ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, the perpendicular bisector of $AC$ intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at $D$ and $E$, respectively. Connect $CD$. If $\angle B=70^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle DCB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle B=70^\circ$ and AB=AC,\\
it follows that $\angle A=180^\circ-2\times70^\circ=40^\circ$,\\
furthermore, since DE is perpendicular bisector of AC,\\
it implies that DA=DC,\\
thus, $\angle ACD=\angle A=40^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle BCD=\angle ACB-\angle ACD=70^\circ-40^\circ=\boxed{30^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; point D is located on side AB, point E is located on side AC, a straight line passes through D and E; line segment CD has been connected, and it can be seen from the figure that CD is located inside angle ACB, dividing angle ACB into two parts, ∠ACD and ∠DCB. Reasoning: It is known that AB=AC, so triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠B=∠C. Also ∠B=70°, therefore ∠ACB=70°, ∠A=180°-70°-70°=40°. Because D is on the perpendicular bisector of AC, DA=DC. Thus in triangle ADC, DA=DC, and the base angles are equal, namely ∠ACD=∠DAC. Since D is on AB, ∠DAC and ∠BAC are the same angle, so ∠DAC=40°, and hence ∠ACD=40°. In the figure CD divides ∠ACB, therefore ∠DCB=∠ACB-∠ACD=70°-40°=30°.
